commands.author: paulpitchford

target.title: fix: external plugin tabs fail under gateway auth
target.body:
Closes #107255

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening an external plugin Control UI tab would see the embedded panel fail with `401 Unauthorized` when the plugin route uses Gateway auth and the Gateway is running in token/password auth mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

External plugin tab descriptors already advertise gateway-local `path` values, and the Control UI should keep rendering those tabs as ordinary sandboxed iframes. This change issues short-lived, signed, HttpOnly plugin-tab cookies after authenticated Control UI read auth, then accepts those cookies only inside the plugin HTTP route auth stage.

The cookie handoff is now bounded in two ways:

- Browser cookie `Path` is scoped to each advertised external plugin tab path.
- The signed payload carries the same route path and the current shared Gateway auth generation, so sibling plugin routes and stale credentials are rejected before runtime scopes are derived.

Direct unauthenticated plugin route requests still return `401`, Gateway credentials are not placed in iframe URLs, and external tab rendering stays a normal `iframe src` load.

## User Impact

Operators can open external plugin Control UI tabs whose HTTP routes are protected with `auth: "gateway"` instead of making those routes public, switching to plugin-managed auth, or putting Gateway credentials in iframe URLs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/control-ui.http.test.ts src/gateway/server.plugin-http-auth.test.ts`
  - Result: `2 passed`, `129 passed`
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`
  - Result: passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/control-ui-plugin-auth-cookie.ts src/gateway/control-ui.http.test.ts src/gateway/control-ui.ts src/gateway/http-auth-utils.ts src/gateway/server-http.ts src/gateway/server.plugin-http-auth.test.ts`
  - Result: passed
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=16384 npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit --pretty false`
  - Result: still fails in pre-existing unrelated `src/plugins/providers.test.ts` readonly tuple errors, not in this gateway/plugin-tab change.

Security regression coverage added:

- Accepts a route-scoped plugin-tab cookie for the matching gateway-auth plugin tab route.
- Accepts child paths under the bound route, for tab assets such as `/secure-hook/assets/app.js`.
- Rejects the cookie on sibling gateway-auth plugin routes.
- Rejects the cookie after the shared Gateway auth generation changes.
- Confirms bootstrap only emits plugin-tab cookies when visible external plugin tab paths exist, and checks `Path=/secure-hook`, `HttpOnly`, and `SameSite=Strict`.

AI-assisted: yes. I used Codex to inspect the Gateway plugin HTTP auth flow, tighten the signed cookie handoff in response to ClawSweeper's security review, add focused regression tests, rebase onto current `main`, and run the validation above. I understand the change: authenticated Control UI read auth mints short-lived route-scoped cookies for visible external plugin tabs, plugin-route auth accepts those cookies only for matching route/current-auth-generation requests, and runtime scopes come from the signed cookie rather than from request headers or URL credentials.
